terra.problem: Aaron being Moses’ brother is a fact from outside the passage and needs its own reference; Numbers 7:8 does not establish it.
The passage does not say the twelve oxen walked to the tabernacle in a line.
The passage does not say the people already had plenty of tents or explain the gifts as a response to having no need for another tent.
The passage says the carts and oxen were given to the Levites for their work, not that they went straight to work.
The passage does not establish that the altar offerings came later than the presentation of the carts and oxen.
The brownie comparison breaks the food rule: cookies are the only food permitted in jokes and comparisons here.
Aaron being Moses’ brother is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
Eleazar being another son of Aaron is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The text says the Kohathites carried the holy objects on their shoulders, not by hand. It also does not say there was nothing for a cart to do.
The text locates the voice between the cherubim above the mercy seat on the ark, not simply as coming from the ark.
